item.description:
Main page with the description, installation and news: [pahaz.8iq.dev/recorder](https://pahaz.8iq.dev/recorder/)
**The first public release of Recorder.** It records your calls and turns them into text right on your Mac. Need a deadline, a number or someone's promise? Find the line instead of replaying an hour of audio.
- **Entirely local.** The recording and the text stay on your computer: no cloud, no account, no bot joining the meeting. - **Any meeting.** Zoom, Meet, Teams or any other app: Recorder captures its sound and your microphone. - **Accurate terms.** Several models check each other, so the text says Postgres, not "постгрес". - **Who said what.** Speakers are told apart by voice, and you name them yourself.
Recognition is for Russian speech, with English terms inside it. The app itself speaks English and Russian.
Requires macOS 15 or later; runs on Apple Silicon and Intel. Free for hobby use; work and business use needs a license.
## Getting started
1. Drag Recorder from the DMG to Applications and open it. 2. Grant two permissions: "Screen & System Audio Recording" and "Microphone". Recorder does not record your screen; macOS requires that permission to hand over system audio. 3. Click "Download models". Without them the app only records.
The text appears in `~/Music/Recorder` next to the audio.
## Automatic updates
From this version on, Recorder finds new releases by itself: once a day it asks `pahaz.8iq.dev` whether a newer version exists and offers to install it. You can turn the check off in the settings, under "Check for updates". Your audio and text are never sent anywhere.
